title: Per-route retention sandbox: simulation, residency-aware TTL previews, and forensic snapshotting
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need confidence that per-route TTLs, residency preferences, and exception rules will behave in production before they commit to enterprise retention policies. Current authoring flows surface TTLs but do not simulate cross-route inheritance, regional residency overrides, or how evidence bundles (forensic snapshots) will be produced for legal/certification audits.

Goal: Build a per-route retention sandbox in the Console that lets PMs/Platform engineers and customers author retention rules, run realistic simulations against sampled request traffic, preview residency-aware TTL effects, and generate a signed forensic snapshot (evidence bundle) that mirrors what would be produced at purge time. The sandbox should be non-destructive, provide exportable artifacts, and integrate with existing evidence/export pipelines.
proposed_solution:
1) UX: a Console page that accepts a set of routes (or tenant), retention rule draft, and simulation window. Shows timeline visualizations of TTL enforcement per artifact class (prompts, responses, request-logs, metrics), residency annotations, and exception hits. 2) Simulation engine: run sampled request traces through current retention-engine logic with a 'dry-run' mode that records when items would be expired, which rule applied, and residency target. 3) Forensic snapshot: produce an exportable, signed evidence bundle that includes hashes of affected artifacts, applied policy fingerprint, simulation inputs, and a proof-of-execution log for audit. 4) Integrations: wire to retention-orchestrator (ENG-51234) and attested-export manifest (ENG-46201), plus KMS signing (security requirement).

Implementation notes: start with a scoped backend spike to reuse retention evaluation code paths; keep simulator bounded (24-72h windows) for first release; front-end will reuse Time Series components from Console and a new "Retention Timeline" card.
acceptance_criteria: Console: author retention draft for a tenant/route and run a simulation against sampled traffic (24h) without modifying production policies
Simulator: outputs per-item enforcement events with rule id, timestamp of expiry, and residency target for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics
Preview UI: displays TTL timelines and highlights routes where inheritance or exceptions changed the expiry outcome
Forensic snapshot: exportable ZIP containing policy fingerprint, signed manifest, per-item hashes, and simulation log; can be validated by an auditor
Security: snapshot signing uses customer KMS key or Redwood-managed HSM according to tenant settings
Integrations: end-to-end test that simulator output can be consumed by evidence-ingest pipeline (ENG-46201)
